What the page is worth — the chart under Your ad's landing page, built 2026-09-16 and wrong at a glance.

Its one job is to teach that capital leaves your account the week you commit it and buys nothing until the site work goes live. It draws the grade correctly and the reader sees a flat row.

Real game throughout: Vella & Co., mid-price performance, writing its own ad, ₹55,000 on the page and ₹25,000 on the size guide at round 0, played to week 5. The page is graded 8 on its own words and the site work adds 2 from week 4.

Why 8 and not 5.

The first mock-ups used a page graded 5 stepping to 7. That is the easy case: 19px of step on a 67px bar. A well-written ad grades higher, and the higher the grade the smaller the step looks — 8 to 10 is 19px on 96px, the worst case the game can produce.

So both options are drawn at 8 → 10. Anything that works here works everywhere below it.

THE OBVIOUS FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT HERE.

Start the bars at 7 instead of 0 and the step becomes enormous. It is also a lie: a 25% gain drawn as a 400% one. Truncating a bar axis is the oldest way to mislead with a chart, and this project's whole claim is that it is honest about what it models.

Both options below keep a full, labelled scale. Neither makes the step bigger — they make it legible.

A — the two points you bought become their own band, in red, the colour this game already uses for you and your changes. The bars still start at zero and still stand for the whole grade, so nothing is exaggerated. It also answers a second question: how much of this grade did I buy?

Smallest change to what is already built.

B — the grade as a step line. RECOMMENDED.

The chart has one job and this is the shape of that job: flat, jump, flat. A reader takes it in before reading the sentence underneath. It is legible without exaggeration because the eye reads a break in a line rather than the area of a bar, and the 0–10 scale stays labelled beside it.

Drawn as a true step, never a slope — the grade does not drift between weeks, it sits still and then moves once. A sloped line would claim a climb the engine never computes.
